newsitem.title: UK: Man charged with N.Irish double police murder.
newsitem.headline: Man charged with N.Irish double police murder.

text.p: Police charged a man on Wednesday with killing two of their colleagues in an IRA ambush that threw Northern Ireland's peace process into turmoil last week.
The suspect, Colin Duffy, 29, from Lurgan town, denied the crimes, a detective inspector told a magistrate later at Craigavon court in County Armagh.
The outlawed Irish Republican Army, which has waged a long war against British rule, admitted killing the two police officers who were shot as they patrolled a street in the busy market town.
His lawyer Rosemary Nelson told reporters outside the court that her client strongly denyied any involvement in killing of the two officers as they patrolled a Lurgan street on June 16.
"He did not take any part in these events. My instructions are to contest the charges strenuously.
The victims were gunned down at close range just before noon and died instantly. They were both married with young families.
The murders set off a wave of revulsion and led to a swift severance by Britain of its tentative contacts with the IRA's Sinn Fein political arm.

British Prime Minister Tony Blair, his Irish counterpart John Bruton and U.S. President Bill Clinton united in condemnation and intensified a clamour for the republican guerrillas to abandon violence forever to win a voice for Sinn Fein in peace talks.
The murders also heightened tension in the run-up to a volatile series of "marching season" parades by pro-British Protestants.
Moderate pro-British Protestant and pro-Irish Catholic politicians accused the IRA of setting out to inflame fears and make the British province more unstable during the contentious parades.

In a keynote parliamentary speech aimed at boosting stalled peace efforts and halting IRA violence, Blair on Wednesday announced details of an Anglo-Irish strategy for the establishment of an international commission that would oversee the scrapping of guerrilla armaments.
Hours before he spoke, police in Belfast foiled a guerrilla ambush after armed men had taken over a house.
One person was arrested and two fully loaded assault rifles, of a type often used in IRA attacks, were seized.
